You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.text:
New task. Hypothesis: rows with 0s have an alternating pattern; the rule might be: complete the alternating 0/5 pattern across the full row. Row 0: "0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5" then "5 5 5..." — pattern 0,5 alternating for 12 cells, then all 5. If extended: 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 5? 19 cells: alternating would give positions 12..18 = 0,5,0,5,0,5,0.

Row 6: cells 5 and 7 are 0: "5 5 5 5 5 0 5 0 5 5..." pattern starting at 5: 0 at odd offsets 5,7,9,11,... so full row: positions 5,7,9,...,17 = 0. That's 0 at odd indices. Consistent with alternating.

Row 10: 0s at 2,4,6,8,10,12 then 5s. Extend: 0 at even positions 2..18? Position 14 currently 5 — pattern 0,5 alternating from index 2: 0 at even indices 2..18.

Row 14: 0s at 5,7,9,11,13,15 then stop. Extend: 0 at odd 5..17.

So rule: each row with 0s, extend the alternating pattern to the full row. Rows without 0s stay all 5.

But is it extension or could it be that each row's pattern is "0 at every other position aligned to grid parity"? Row 0 starts with 0 at even; row 10 zeros at even too; rows 6 and 14 zeros at odd. So alignment varies per row — determined by the existing zeros. Extension hypothesis fits all.

Risk: maybe instead zeros pattern alternates per row in a specific phase and pattern only extends to certain length. Cost of a wrong guess: 1. I could request a demo first to validate (cost 1). Given uncertainty, requesting one demo seems wise — but if my hypothesis is right, a demo costs 1 too. Wrong submission also costs 1 and I get no explanation. Demo gives more info. With 8 attempts and 8 demos, requesting 1 demo is safe and cheap. I'll request a demo.

Demo: row 4: 1s at positions 4,6,8; output: 1 2 1 2 1 — fill gaps between 1s with 2. Row 10: 1s at 8,10; output fills gap at 9 with 2.

So rule: between consecutive 0s (in test, color 0 plays role of "1", 5 is bg), fill gaps of one cell with... in demo the alternate color is 2 = the "other color". In test, rows have 0s with 5 in between; filling gaps would give 0 5 0 5... but they're already 5. Hmm.

In demo: pattern is 1 X 1 where X is 7 → becomes 2. In test: 0 5 0 → the in-between already 5. What's the "other color" in test? Maybe the pattern extends: alternation continues to the right edge? Demo row 4 output does NOT extend: stays 1 2 1 2 1 7... So no extension. So demo says: only fill single-cell gaps between markers with color 2.

But test rows already have 5 between 0s — no change? That can't be, output must differ... unless the alternate color in test is different. Test row 0: 0 5 0 5 0 5 ... — alternating 0/5 with 5 as filler. Filling gaps would make them something else. What color? In demo, 2 is not present in input. In test input, colors present: 0 and 5. The fill color must be 2 too? Fill the gaps between 0s with 2?

Demo: gaps between 1s filled with 2. Test: gaps between 0s currently 5; fill with 2? So output rows: 0 2 0 2 0 ... replacing the 5s between 0s with 2.

Row 0 test: 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 0 5 then 5s. Gaps between consecutive 0s: positions 1,3,5,7,9,11 → become 2. Row 6: 0 at 5,7 → gap at 6 → 2. Row 10: 0s at 2,4,6,8,10,12 → gaps 3,5,7,9,11 → 2. Row 14: 0s at 5,7,9,11,13,15 → gaps 6,8,10,12,14 → 2.
